claim: Expansion microscopy (ExM) enables nanoscale imaging using a standard confocal microscope through the physical, isotropic expansion of fixed immunolabeled specimens.
source: Expansion microscopy (ExM) enables nanoscale imaging using a standard confocal microscope through the physical, isotropic expansion of fixed immunolabeled specimens.
evidence: This is a foundational statement about ExM technology that is established in the field and cited throughout the manuscript.

claim: Current ExM methods limit the number of samples that can be processed simultaneously.
source: ExM is widely employed to image proteins, nucleic acids, and lipid membranes in single cells; however, current methods limit the number of samples that can be processed simultaneously.
evidence: This statement identifies a limitation in existing methods that motivates the development of HiExM.

claim: HiExM enables ~4.2 x expansion of cells within individual wells, across multiple wells, and between plates.
source: Our method enables ~4.2 x expansion of cells within individual wells, across multiple wells, and between plates.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental measurements presented in Figure 2h.

claim: HiExM can be combined with high-throughput confocal imaging platforms to greatly improve the ease and scalability of image acquisition.
source: We also demonstrate that HiExM can be combined with high-throughput confocal imaging platforms to greatly improve the ease and scalability of image acquisition.
evidence: This claim is supported by the use of the Opera Phenix system described in the Results section and Figure 2.

claim: HiExM shows a dose-dependent effect of doxorubicin on nuclear DNA that is not observed in unexpanded cardiomyocytes.
source: We show a dose-dependent effect on nuclear DNA that is not observed in unexpanded CMs, suggesting that HiExM improves the detection of cellular phenotypes in response to drug treatment.
evidence: This finding is supported by the analysis presented in Figure 3, showing differences in Hoechst signal patterns at the nuclear periphery.

claim: Super-resolution microscopy methods such as SIM, STORM, and STED require specialized expertise and costly reagents and microscopes.
source: Super-resolution microscopy methods such as structured illumination microscopy (SIM), stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM), and stimulated emission depletion microscopy (STED) enable nanoscale imaging of specimens (Gustafsson, 2000; Hell and Wichmann, 1994; Rust et al., 2006). However, these approaches require specialized expertise, costly reagents and microscopes.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to the original super-resolution microscopy papers and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: ExM is an inexpensive and accessible method that resolves fluorescently labeled structures at subcellular resolution by isotropically enlarging specimens within a swellable polyelectrolyte hydrogel.
source: ExM is an inexpensive and accessible method that similarly resolves fluorescently labeled structures at subcellular resolution by isotropically enlarging specimens within a swellable polyelectrolyte hydrogel (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the original ExM paper by Chen et al., 2015.

claim: Sample processing and imaging in super-resolution microscopy and ExM require time-consuming manual manipulation, limiting throughput.
source: Super-resolution imaging and ExM are critical tools that are widely used in biological research; however, sample processing and imaging require time-consuming manual manipulation, limiting throughput.
evidence: This statement identifies a limitation that motivates the development of HiExM.

claim: Adapting standard ExM to a 96-well plate requires the reproducible delivery of a small volume of gel solution to each well (<1 µL compared to ~200 µL/sample for slide-based ExM).
source: Adapting standard ExM to a 96-well plate requires the reproducible delivery of a small volume of gel solution to each well (<1 µL compared to ~200 µL/sample for slide-based ExM).
evidence: This is a technical requirement identified by the authors for adapting ExM to 96-well plates.

claim: The small volume of gel solution is necessary to allow complete gel expansion within the size constraints of wells in a 96-well plate.
source: This small volume is necessary to allow complete gel expansion within the size constraints of wells in a 96-well plate.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the physical constraints of the 96-well plate format.

claim: The HiExM device retains small liquid droplets when dipped into a reservoir of monomeric expansion gel solution.
source: To achieve this goal, we engineered a device that retains small liquid droplets when dipped into a reservoir of monomeric expansion gel solution.
evidence: This describes the function of the engineered device, supported by Figure 1.

claim: The retention of the gel solution is mediated by a series of reticulated grooves at the end of a cylindrical post which allows for the formation of a pendant droplet.
source: The retention of the gel solution is mediated by a series of reticulated grooves at the end of a cylindrical post which allows for the formation of a pendant droplet (Figure 1c).
evidence: This mechanism is described in the text and shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Each post retains ~230 nL of gel solution as measured by the mass of liquid accumulated on all post tips of a single device after dipping.
source: We estimate that each post retains ~230 nL of gel solution as measured by the mass of liquid accumulated on all post tips of a single device after dipping (Supplementary methods).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement described in the text and detailed in supplementary methods.

claim: The small volume of gel solution delivered to each well by the device forms a toroidal droplet where the inner surface is molded by the conical surface of the post-tip and the outer surface is constrained by surface tension.
source: The small volume of gel solution delivered to each well by the device forms a toroidal droplet where the inner surface is molded by the conical surface of the post-tip and the outer surface is constrained by surface tension (Figure 1c and d).
evidence: This describes the geometry of the gel droplet, supported by Figure 1c and d.

claim: The toroidal gel enables isotropic gel expansion within the well constraints while allowing for easy device removal.
source: The toroidal gel enables isotropic gel expansion within the well constraints while allowing for easy device removal because the inner surface of the gel expands outward away from the conical post-tip, effectively detaching the gel from the device.
evidence: This explains the functional advantage of the toroidal geometry.

claim: ProExM using APS and TEMED to initiate gel polymerization resulted in inconsistent polymerization and expansion.
source: Although we observed gel formation across wells, polymerization and expansion were inconsistent, likely due to inconsistent radical formation and rapid evaporation of the small volume relative to the rate of polymerization (Figure 1—animation 1).
evidence: This observation is supported by Figure 1—animation 1 and led to testing alternative polymerization methods.

claim: Irgacure 2959 allowed reproducible gel formation and expansion when compared to either APS/TEMED or other photoinitiators.
source: We found that Irgacure 2959 allowed reproducible gel formation and expansion when compared to either APS/TEMED or other photoinitiators (Figure 1—animation 2).
evidence: This finding is supported by Figure 1—animation 2 and comparison data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: CF dyes are robust against bleaching in HiExM and result in reproducible signal retention.
source: Although we observed bleaching of AlexaFluor dyes in our Irgacure 2959 photopolymerized gels, Cyanine-based Fluorescent (CF) dyes are robust against bleaching in HiExM and result in reproducible signal retention (Figure 1—figure supplement 4; Jiang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: 50 µg/mL AcX and 1 U/mL ProteinaseK were most consistent for A549 cells.
source: We also titrated AcX and ProteinaseK to optimize signal retention in HiExM and found the 50 µg/mL AcX and 1 U/mL ProteinaseK were most consistent for A549 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This optimization result is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The Opera Phenix system allowed autonomous capture of images across the entire plate at a resolution of ~115 nm compared to ~463 nm for unexpanded samples.
source: This approach allowed autonomous capture of images across the entire plate at a resolution of ~115 nm compared to ~463 nm for unexpanded samples using the same microscope, objective (63 X, 1.15NA water immersion), and imaging wavelength (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This resolution measurement is supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and decorrelation analysis.

claim: Image resolution was calculated using a decorrelation analysis.
source: Image resolution was calculated using a decorrelation analysis (Descloux et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the method used for resolution calculation, supported by citation.

claim: The average percent error (up to 40 μm measurement length post-expansion) was not correlated with distance from the gel center (R2=0.003).
source: The average percent error (up to 40 μm measurement length post-expansion) was plotted against the distance from the center of the gel (Figure 2e). Our analysis found no correlation (R2=0.003) between expansion error and distance from the gel center.
evidence: This statistical finding is supported by the data presented in Figure 2e.

claim: Expansion error was highly consistent when comparing wells across multiple plates (average = 3.68%), comparable to slide-based ExM.
source: Expansion error was also highly consistent when comparing wells across multiple plates (average = 3.68%), comparable to slide-based ExM (Figure 2f; Chen et al., 2015; Tillberg et al., 2016).
evidence: This finding is supported by data in Figure 2f and comparison to published ExM methods.

claim: Photoinitiation resulted in markedly lower spatial errors compared to APS and TEMED polymerization chemistry.
source: Moreover, the calculated error showed that photoinitiation resulted in markedly lower spatial errors compared to APS and TEMED polymerization chemistry (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This comparison is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Cell confluency did not affect image distortion as measured by NRR.
source: Analyzing cell seeding densities also showed that cell confluency did not affect image distortion as measured by NRR (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This finding is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The average expansion factor of gels sampled across three plates was 4.16+/-0.394.
source: The average expansion factor of gels sampled across three plates was 4.16+/-0.394 (Figure 2h), consistent with proExM (Tillberg et al., 2016).
evidence: This quantitative measurement is supported by data in Figure 2h and comparison to published proExM.

claim: The expansion factor was highly reproducible across different regions of the gel.
source: We found that the expansion factor was highly reproducible across different regions of the gel confirming robust expansion using our method (Figure 2g).
evidence: This finding is supported by data in Figure 2g.

claim: There were statistically significant differences between expansion factor distributions across three well plates.
source: We next compared the distributions of expansion factors across three well plates by ANOVA and found statistically significant differences between expansion factor distributions.
evidence: This statistical finding is based on ANOVA analysis of the data presented in Figure 2h.

claim: The expansion factor is somewhat variable between gels and plates, attributed primarily to the small size of the gels making them vulnerable to the effects of evaporation.
source: Thus, while uniform within gels, the expansion factor is somewhat variable between gels and plates. We attribute these differences primarily to the small size of the gels, making them vulnerable to the effects of evaporation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed variability with a proposed mechanism.

claim: Commonly used doxorubicin concentrations in in vitro cardiotoxicity studies range between 0.1 to 10 μM.
source: Commonly used dox concentrations in in vitro cardiotoxicity studies range between 0.1 to 10 μM, depending on experimental goals (Maillet et al., 2016; Yu et al., 2020; Zhao and Zhang, 2017; Stefanova et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published cardiotoxicity studies.

claim: Changes in nuclear morphology and DNA damage are associated with cellular stress and apoptosis, commonly observed at high doxorubicin concentrations (>200 nM) in in vitro studies using conventional microscopy.
source: For example, changes in nuclear morphology as well as DNA damage are associated with cellular stress and apoptosis, which are commonly observed at high dox concentrations (>200 nM) in in vitro studies using conventional microscopy (Maillet et al., 2016; Yu et al., 2020; Zhao and Zhang, 2017; Stefanova et al., 2023; Gewirtz, 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: HiExM revealed a peak of Hoechst intensity at the edge of the nucleus that is not resolved in pre-expansion images.
source: Notably, HiExM revealed a peak of Hoechst intensity at the edge of the nucleus that is not resolved in pre-expansion images (Figure 3f).
evidence: This observation is supported by the data presented in Figure 3f.

claim: Post-expansion, the gradient slopes on both sides of the peak showed a significant increase at dox concentrations as low as 10 nM compared to DMSO, whereas no trend is observed in pre-expansion images.
source: Post-expansion, the gradient slopes on both sides of the peak showed a significant increase at dox concentrations as low as 10 nM compared to DMSO, whereas no trend is observed in pre-expansion images (Figure 3g).
evidence: This finding is supported by the analysis presented in Figure 3g.

claim: Hoechst intensity at the nuclear edge showed a significant increase in curvature at 10 nM dox compared to DMSO, whereas no significant difference is observed using conventional confocal microscopy.
source: These data also showed a significant increase in Hoechst intensity at 10 nM dox compared to DMSO, whereas no significant difference is observed using conventional confocal microscopy (Figure 3i).
evidence: This finding is supported by the curvature analysis presented in Figure 3h and i.

claim: For both the outer gradient slope and peak curvature, values decrease from 100 nM to 1 µM dox, consistent with increased chromatin condensation associated with apoptosis typically observed at higher dox concentrations.
source: We note that, for both the outer gradient slope and peak curvature, values decrease from 100 nM to 1 µM dox, consistent with increased chromatin condensation associated with apoptosis typically observed at higher dox concentrations (Zhao and Zhang, 2017; Toné et al., 2007).
evidence: This observation is supported by data in Figure 3 and citations to published studies on apoptosis.

claim: CMs treated with increasing concentrations of H2O2 did not show similar differences in Hoechst patterns.
source: In contrast, CMs treated with increasing concentrations of H2O2, another cellular stressor, did not show similar differences in Hoechst patterns (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This control experiment is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: HiExM is a simple and inexpensive method that can increase the throughput of expansion microscopy.
source: Our work demonstrates that HiExM is a simple and inexpensive method that can increase the throughput of expansion microscopy.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the overall findings of the study.

claim: Another recent method reports a scalable ExM-based method with comparable throughput, albeit this approach requires the use of a custom cell culture microplate and manual imaging.
source: Another recent method also reports a scalable ExM-based method with comparable throughput, albeit this approach requires the use of a custom cell culture microplate and manual imaging (Xie et al., 2023)
evidence: This comparison is supported by citation to Xie et al., 2023.

claim: The HiExM device is fabricated with CNC milling, a common fabrication technique available in most academic settings.
source: Our device is fabricated with CNC milling, a common fabrication technique available in most academic settings, making our method widely accessible.
evidence: This describes the fabrication method and its accessibility.

claim: The HiExM device can be produced by injection molding which can further extend its accessibility and distribution in research settings.
source: The HiExM device can also be produced by injection molding which can further extend its accessibility and distribution in research settings.
evidence: This describes an alternative fabrication method demonstrated in Figure 1—figure supplement 7.

claim: The HiExM device has been adapted to fit cell culture plates of varying dimensions including a 24-well plate which can accommodate greater expansion and significantly higher resolution.
source: We have also adapted our device to fit cell culture plates of varying dimensions including a 24-well plate which can accommodate greater expansion and significantly higher resolution (Figure 1—figure supplement 7; Damstra et al., 2022).
evidence: This adaptation is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 7 and cited to Damstra et al., 2022.

claim: The use of photoinitiation with irgacure caused signal loss to varying degrees depending on the fluorophore.
source: In this work, we found that the use of photoinitiation with irgacure caused signal loss for to varying degrees depending on the fluorophore; coupled with the signal dilution inherent to the expansion process, signal intensity is an important consideration when using HiExM.
evidence: This observation is based on the photobleaching data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The HiExM platform is amenable to other photo-active expansion chemistries such as Photo-ExM chemistry which does not require CF dyes or an anoxic environment.
source: Our platform is amenable to other photo-active expansion chemistries such as the Photo-ExM chemistry which does not require CF dyes or an anoxic environment (Figure 3—figure supplement 6; Blatchley et al., 2022; Günay et al., 2023).
evidence: This compatibility is demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 6 and supported by citations.

claim: HiExM is fully compatible with autonomous imaging, allowing data acquisition of thousands of cells within a day.
source: Another advantage of HiExM is that it is fully compatible with autonomous imaging, allowing data acquisition of thousands of cells within a day.
evidence: This capability is demonstrated through the use of the Opera Phenix system described in the Results section.

claim: HiExM achieved a resolution of ~115 nm in a 96-well culture plate using a 63 x water immersion objective with a 1.15 numerical aperture.
source: HiExM achieved a resolution of ~115 nm in a 96-well culture plate using a 63 x water immersion objective with a 1.15 numerical aperture.
evidence: This resolution measurement is supported by the decorrelation analysis described in the Results section.

claim: By employing microscopes with a higher numerical aperture, the HiExM platform can achieve significantly greater resolution.
source: By employing microscopes with a higher numerical aperture, we expect our platform can achieve significantly greater resolution.
evidence: This is a prediction based on optical principles.

claim: HiExM error measurements are similar to proExM.
source: We also show that HiExM error measurements are similar to proExM and suggest that expansion distortions should be considered for robust data interpretation.
evidence: This comparison is supported by the NRR analysis in Figure 2 and citations to proExM papers.

claim: Gels deposited in HiExM cover ~1.1 mm2 of the well surface to accommodate the expanded gel, and do not include cells outside the gel footprint.
source: Note that gels deposited in HiExM cover ~1.1 mm2 of the well surface to accommodate the expanded gel, and do not include cells outside the gel footprint.
evidence: This is a description of the gel coverage area shown in Figure 1g.

claim: The device was designed with three different post lengths where the four center posts are the longest, the two pairs of posts on the ends near the pressure struts are the shortest, and the middle posts are an intermediate length.
source: The device was designed with three different post lengths where the four center posts are the longest, the two pairs of posts on the ends near the pressure struts are the shortest, and the middle posts are an intermediate length.
evidence: This design feature is described in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: When the device is inserted into the well plate, the center four posts contact the culture surface first.
source: When the device is inserted into the well plate, the center four posts contact the culture surface first.
evidence: This describes the sequential contact mechanism shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: As downward pressure is applied to the ends of the device, the spine of the device bends at the notches such that all posts contact the plate.
source: As downward pressure is applied to the ends of the device (by the user pressing down above the pressure struts), the spine of the device bends at the notches such that all posts contact the plate.
evidence: This describes the bending mechanism shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: These design features allow for the reproducible deposition of gel solution droplets and the reproducible formation of toroidal gels within the well constraints.
source: These design features allow for the reproducible deposition of gel solution droplets and the reproducible formation of toroidal gels within the well constraints.
evidence: This is a summary of the functional advantages of the design features described in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The use of photoinitiation HiExM allows for one-step polymerization.
source: The use of photoinitiation HiExM as described in Methods allows for one-step polymerization.
evidence: This is described in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B and the Methods section.

claim: HiExM can be used with cells cultured in commercially available 96-well plates.
source: HiExM can be used with cells cultured in commercially available 96-well plates.
evidence: This is described in Figure 1—figure supplement 3 and the Methods section.

claim: Photo-ExM does not require an anoxic environment for gel deposition and polymerization, improving the ease of use of HiExM.
source: Photo-ExM does not require an anoxic environment for gel deposition and polymerization, improving the ease of use of HiExM.
evidence: This advantage is described in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: HiExM is compatible with additional fluorophores when combined with Photo-ExM.
source: Mitochondria were stained with an Alexa 647 conjugated secondary antibody, demonstrating that HiExM is compatible with additional fluorophores when combined with Photo-ExM.
evidence: This compatibility is demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: In some cases, residual Hoechst signal underneath expanded cells was observed due to digested cells that were incompletely removed during wash steps during the expansion process.
source: In some cases, we observed residual Hoechst signal underneath expanded cells due to digested cells that were incompletely removed during wash steps during the expansion process (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This observation is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: Residual Hoechst signal does not impact the interpretation of results.
source: This signal does not impact the interpretation of results.
evidence: This is an assessment by the authors based on their analysis.

claim: Optimum signal-to-noise was found at concentrations of 50 µg/mL AcX and 1 U/mL ProteinaseK.
source: Optimum signal-to-noise was found at concentrations of 50 µg/mL AcX and 1 U/mL ProteinaseK.
evidence: This optimization result is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The vertical component of expansion increases the depth of the sample, necessitating more optical z-slices to image the full depth of the sample.
source: For example, the vertical component of expansion increases the depth of the sample, necessitating more optical z-slices to image the full depth of the sample.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of 3D expansion.

claim: Expansion effectively decreases the field-of-view due to increasing sample size, necessitating the acquisition of more images to analyze the same number of cells at lower resolution.
source: Moreover, expansion effectively decreases the field-of-view due to increasing sample size, necessitating the acquisition of more images to analyze the same number of cells at lower resolution.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of physical expansion.

claim: The PreciScan plug-in in the Harmony analysis software was used to accurately target regions of interest based on Hoechst staining to reduce acquisition times at higher magnification.
source: We used the PreciScan plug-in in the Harmony analysis software to first accurately target regions of interest based on Hoechst staining to reduce acquisition times at higher magnification.
evidence: This describes the imaging workflow used in the study.

claim: Plates were imaged at 5 x across entire wells and the coordinates of nuclei for each well were stored and used to direct the 63 x magnification objective to the relevant fields of view.
source: Briefly, we imaged plates at 5 x across entire wells and stored the coordinates of nuclei for each well. These coordinates were then used to direct the 63 x magnification objective to the relevant fields of view.
evidence: This describes the automated imaging workflow.

claim: Prior to expansion, 61 fields were imaged at 63 x around the center of the gel.
source: Prior to expansion, 61 fields were imaged at 63 x around the center of the gel.
evidence: This describes the pre-expansion imaging protocol shown in Figure 2b.

claim: After expansion, 12 fields were imaged at 20 x magnification.
source: After expansion, 12 fields were imaged at 20 x magnification.
evidence: This describes the post-expansion imaging protocol shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Gels did not maintain a fixed position pre- and post-expansion.
source: Although we observed that gels did not maintain a fixed position pre- and post- expansion, close inspection of the images allowed us to align their orientations.
evidence: This observation is based on the image analysis described in the Results section.

claim: Only a small number of outliers (>3 s.d.) were observed in any given well (<2 instances per gel across six gels).
source: In fact, we observed only a small number of outliers (>3 s.d.) in any given well (<2 instances per gel across six gels).
evidence: This statistical observation is based on the NRR analysis presented in Figure 2.

claim: Outliers are not expected to affect biological interpretation.
source: These outliers are not expected to affect biological interpretation.
evidence: This is an assessment by the authors based on the low frequency of outliers.

claim: Outliers closer to the center of the gel likely occur when the device post is not in full contact with the well surface, resulting in a higher volume of gel at the center that resists gel swelling under the device.
source: The outliers, which are closer to the center of the gel, likely occur when the device post is not in full contact with the well surface, resulting in a higher volume of gel at the center that resists gel swelling under the device (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism for the observed outliers, supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Only a small number of image fields (7 of 58) had an average percent error above 6% (maximum 6.78%).
source: We observed only a small number of image fields (7 of 58) with an average percent error above 6% (maximum 6.78%).
evidence: This statistical observation is based on the NRR analysis.

claim: Images of expanded cells show a higher effective resolution due to an increase in the distance between the fluorescent molecules.
source: Images of expanded cells show a higher effective resolution due to an increase in the distance between the fluorescent molecules.
evidence: This is a fundamental principle of expansion microscopy.

claim: There has been success in increasing the throughput of certain super-resolution microscopy techniques, but these methods require highly specialized equipment and expertise which limits the accessibility of these tools.
source: Although there has been success in increasing the throughput of certain super-resolution microscopy techniques, these methods require highly specialized equipment and expertise which limits the accessibility of these tools (Holden et al., 2014; Gunkel et al., 2014; Mahecic et al., 2020; Xie et al., 2023).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published work on high-throughput super-resolution methods.

claim: HiExM combines parallel sample processing and automated high-content confocal imaging in a standard 96-well cell culture plate.
source: To circumvent these limitations, we developed HiExM that combines parallel sample processing and automated high-content confocal imaging in a standard 96-well cell culture plate.
evidence: This describes the key features of the HiExM platform.

claim: The known pro-apoptotic effects of doxorubicin strongly suggest that the observed changes in Hoechst patterns correlate with these changes.
source: Although direct evidence specifically linking dox to increased DNA condensation at the nuclear periphery is limited, the known pro-apoptotic effects of dox strongly suggest that our observations correlate with these changes (Maillet et al., 2016; Zhao and Zhang, 2017; Mobaraki et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on published literature about doxorubicin's effects.

claim: HiExM can detect early alterations in response to dox treatment using the Hoechst signal.
source: Thus, we suggest that HiExM can detect early alterations in response to dox treatment using the Hoechst signal, setting the stage for further investigation to understand the consequences across a range of drugs and conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the doxorubicin experiment results presented in Figure 3.

claim: HiExM can detect subtle cellular changes compared to standard confocal microscopy that could improve the resolution of drug screening approaches.
source: Overall, our analysis demonstrates the ability of HiExM to detect subtle cellular changes compared to standard confocal microscopy that could improve the resolution of drug screening approaches.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the doxorubicin experiment comparing pre- and post-expansion imaging.

claim: HiExM broadens the application of ExM as a tool for scalable super-resolution imaging in biological research applications.
source: Our method broadens the application of ExM as a tool for scalable super-resolution imaging in biological research applications.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the overall contribution of the work.

claim: Recent innovative work developed a microplate-based ExM protocol that maintains hydrogel geometry and orientation and improves coordinate-based imaging to accurately assess distortions with ease.
source: Recent innovative work that developed a microplate-based ExM protocol maintains hydrogel geometry and orientation improves coordinate-based imaging to accurately assess distortions with ease (Seehra et al., 2023).
evidence: This describes related work cited from Seehra et al., 2023.

claim: Another recent work used micropatterning to apply expandable protein grids to coverslips for local expansion factor measurement, which could be adapted to HiExM to enable expansion measurements in large datasets where non-rigid registration is impractical.
source: Another recent work used micropatterning to apply expandable protein grids to coverslips for local expansion factor measurement. This method could be adapted to HiExM to enable expansion measurements in large datasets where non-rigid registration is impractical (Damstra et al., 2023)
evidence: This describes related work from Damstra et al., 2023 and suggests a potential future application.

claim: HiExM is an accessible nanoscale imaging platform designed for scalable sample preparation and autonomous imaging.
source: Taken together, HiExM is an accessible nanoscale imaging platform designed for scalable sample preparation and autonomous imaging, broadening the use of ExM in biological research and pharmaceutical applications.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the overall contribution and potential applications of HiExM.

claim: Imaging one full 96-well plate (60 wells total to avoid outer wells) requires 3 to 64 hr depending on the combination of parameters used.
source: Therefore, imaging one full 96-well plate (60 wells total to avoid outer wells) requires 3 to 64 hr depending on the combination of parameters used.
evidence: This describes the time requirements for imaging based on the parameters described in the Methods section.

claim: Non-rigid registration was performed using a custom MATLAB analysis pipeline as described by Chen et al., 2015.
source: Non-rigid registration was performed using a custom MATLAB analysis pipeline as described (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the computational method used for distortion analysis, supported by citation.

claim: Pre and post-expansion images are coarsely aligned using the TurboReg plugin for ImageJ.
source: Briefly, pre and post-expansion images are coarsely aligned using the TurboReg plugin for ImageJ (Jiang et al., 2021).
evidence: This describes a step in the image analysis workflow, supported by citation.

claim: B-spline-based registration package in MATLAB was used to do non-rigid registration between the images.
source: B-spline-based registration package in MATLAB was used to do non-rigid registration between the images.
evidence: This describes the computational tool used for NRR analysis.

claim: The average percent error up to 40 µm measurement length (as measured after expansion) was used to synthesize NRR curves into single points.
source: To synthesize these curves into single points (as represented in Figure 2c–f), The average percent error up to 40 µm measurement length (as measured after expansion) was used.
evidence: This describes the method for summarizing NRR data.

claim: The midplane of each nucleus was manually identified as the plane with the largest nuclear cross-sectional area.
source: Image stacks of Hoechst-stained nuclei were compiled and the midplane of each nucleus was manually identified as the plane with the largest nuclear cross-sectional area.
evidence: This describes the method for selecting the appropriate optical plane for analysis.

claim: Images containing no nucleus or clearly distorted nuclei were omitted from the analysis.
source: Images containing no nucleus or clearly distorted nuclei were omitted from the analysis.
evidence: This describes the quality control criteria for image selection.

claim: Significance was determined using a two-sample t-test (p<0.05).
source: Significance was determined using a two-sample t-test (p<0.05).
evidence: This describes the statistical test used for the nuclear periphery analysis.
